attackSurface.publicPages: Legacy public site plus typed CMS EN/FR/ES page/product/editorial routes and public sitemap/robots; new Worker publishes projected visible content into escaped HTML/JSON.
attackSurface.dynamicRoutes: GET /api/cms, /api/cms/document; authenticated GET /api/admin/content, /content/revisions, /content/revisions/N; PUT /content/draft; POST /content/validate, /content/publish, /content/rollback; POST /api/admin/media; GET/HEAD /api/admin/media/<key>; GET /api/admin/recovery/backup, /recovery/orphans; POST /recovery/restore; public GET/HEAD /media/upload-<uuid>.<jpg|png|webp>.
attackSurface.authSession: Cloudflare Access RS256 assertions, issuer/audience and subject/email allowlist; no local passwords, sessions or frontend auth authority. Synthetic local signer/JWKS are scratch-only harness, production entry unchanged.
attackSurface.databaseStorage: Singleton site in D1; append-only revisions with version-CAS transactional pointers; R2 uploads private by application design; durable D1 upload reservations. Legacy production KV fixed read-only key.
attackSurface.uploads: Raw JPEG/PNG/WebP only, 8 MiB streamed cap, 8192 dimension and 12M pixel max, strict containers + Images decode/re-encode, UUID object names, protected previews/current publication-gated public reads.
attackSurface.outboundFetch: Restricted configured Access cert endpoint only; fixed ASSETS service binding requests. Browser external HTTPS links/images are not server URL imports.
attackSurface.adminPrivate: /admin[/...] and every /api/admin path gated before fallback; same shared permission for every allowlisted editor, including backup and publication. No tenant/customer accounts.
attackSurface.paymentsWebhooks: None. Product prices are editorial display; booking prepares WhatsApp inquiry without server submission/payment or stored customer bookings.
attackSurface.aiSpend: No AI endpoint; D1/R2/Images and revision/backup CPU/storage are spend-sensitive. Upload budgets are durable, other CMS read/write rates and revision growth are not bounded.
attackSurface.logging: Worker no console logging; generic errors; private actor subjects in immutable revision/accounting records. Provider/Access/CI log access/retention unknown.
attackSurface.recovery: Authenticated export contains documents + media hash manifest, NOT object bytes; restore validates manifests/objects then adds draft only; orphan route dry-run only; local stopped-state snapshot includes D1/R2 bytes with symlink/overlap/integrity checks. No remote offsite backup/restore operations proven.
attackSurface.ciArtifacts: No tracked CI workflow. Vite build + Worker dist assets; ignore dist/.wrangler/logs/.cms-backups; .dev.vars* not ignored. Fresh isolated parent build succeeded but final release output manifest scan remains open.

limits: Security launch-filter audit, not a penetration test or production-readiness certification.

No commits, pushes, deployment, remote resource/config/auth change, production writes or owner-preview writes. Auditor only wrote the two report files; tests used in-memory or isolated temporary state.

Cloudflare Access/IdP sessions, password recovery, IAM, actual private bucket settings, secret storage, logs/retention, staging hosts, default vendor accounts, account quotas/costs and scheduled production backups were not inspected/configured.
No production POST/PUT/DELETE/OPTIONS or credentialed/private-data requests; production GET bodies retained only as hashes/shapes/header names, no personal body values or secrets.

One follow-up uncustomized Python root GET returned HTTP 403; retry using the same explicit read-only audit headers as the successful initial sweep succeeded. No authentication bypass, token use or state-changing workaround.

Working tree is shared/dirty. Hashes pin security files at audit snapshot; concurrent later source changes require focused/full re-audit. Parent browser proof was still unresolved when this report was prepared.
